scenarios.title: Turbine bracket — service fracture
scenarios.subtitle: Casting · hydrogen porosity · the stage story

findings.title: Crack origin
findings.detail: The fracture begins 0.4 mm below the root fillet, not at the surface. The initiation site is a casting void.

findings.title: Tool mark
findings.detail: A machining ridge from pass 3 sits 7 mm from the crack. It is a real surface defect, but the crack path ignores it.

findings.title: Gas porosity cluster
findings.detail: Six voids under the fillet. Largest void 0.8 mm, aligned with the crack path. Hydrogen level ran 0.86 ppm above baseline.

batch.notes: Accepted on a 1.4 ppm hydrogen deviation. Supplier note: 'within measurement tolerance'.

maintenance.note: Seal showed heat damage. Furnace not re-validated for hydrogen pick-up after the repair.
Valve response lag logged at 4 s. No follow-up measurement.
Insert changed on schedule. Surface finish in tolerance.

history.notes: Ridge at the fillet, surface crack.

hypotheses.label: Tool mark / operator error
hypotheses.summary: A machining ridge sits near the root fillet and the previous shift changed the finishing insert. This is the most common answer for a fillet crack and the strongest match to surface evidence.
hypotheses.note: Plausible because a real ridge is visible 7 mm from the crack.

hypotheses.label: Gas porosity in the casting
hypotheses.summary: Hydrogen picked up during the hold formed a void cluster under the fillet. The largest void sits on the crack path. Batch B-2291 was accepted on a hydrogen exception.
hypotheses.note: Evidence is subsurface; it only appears after the depth reveal.

hypotheses.label: Quench cracking
hypotheses.summary: Quench bath temperature dropped 16 °C below setpoint. The steep thermal gradient can open a hairline crack from any existing void.
hypotheses.note: A contributing mechanism, not the initiator.

hypotheses.label: Contaminated material batch
hypotheses.summary: Batch B-2291 came in at 1.9 ppm hydrogen against a 1.4 ppm limit. The supplier granted a deviation. Other parts from the batch have not failed, which weakens this as a standalone cause.

evidence.title: Crack origin at the root fillet
evidence.detail: Optical macro, 2.6x. The beach marks radiate from a point 0.4 mm below the surface.

evidence.title: Porosity cluster under the fillet
evidence.detail: X-ray CT slice. Six voids, largest 0.8 mm, aligned with the crack path.

evidence.title: Machining ridge, pass 3
evidence.detail: Surface topography. 0.05 mm deep, 7 mm from the crack origin. Surface-only feature.

evidence.title: Hydrogen above baseline
evidence.detail: Melt hydrogen averaged 2.04 ppm through the cast window against a 1.18 ppm baseline (9.6 sigma).

evidence.title: Quench bath ran cold
evidence.detail: Quench temperature fell to 42 °C against a 58 °C setpoint. Cold quench raises the thermal gradient at the fillet.

evidence.title: Material batch B-2291
evidence.detail: Supplier certificate reports 1.9 ppm hydrogen at the ingot. Batch was accepted on a 1.4 ppm limit exception.

evidence.title: Furnace door seal replaced
evidence.detail: Seal replaced 12 days before the failure. Degraded seal explains the hydrogen pick-up during the hold.

evidence.title: Operator note, shift B
evidence.detail: Operator flagged a 'different pour sound' at 05:50 and logged no alarm. No process change was made.

evidence.title: Case 0398 — same batch family
evidence.detail: Hydrogen porosity initiated a quench crack on the same fillet. Approved cause: gas porosity. 4.1 h to resolve.

evidence.title: Case 0361 — tool mark false lead
evidence.detail: A machining ridge was proposed and rejected: the crack origin was subsurface. Confirmed gas porosity.

evidence.title: Crack starts below the surface
evidence.detail: Depth measurement: initiation at 0.4 mm. Tool marks are surface-only and cannot initiate this crack.

report.title: Root cause report — RC-0417
report.summary: Gas porosity in the casting initiated a quench crack, which grew in service to a brittle fracture of the root fillet.

sections.heading: Finding
sections.body:
Gas porosity in the casting initiated a quench crack, which grew in service to a brittle fracture of the root fillet.

Causal chain: Gas porosity -> Quench crack -> Service growth -> Failure.

sections.heading: Evidence reviewed
sections.body: Reviewed: camera 06 macro image, x-ray CT slice, 6-hour machine window for furnace 2 and the quench line, batch B-2291 certificate, 12 matching historical cases, and the last 90 days of maintenance records.

sections.heading: Corrective action
sections.body:
1. Quarantine the remainder of batch B-2291 and re-test hydrogen on three sample castings.
2. Replace the furnace door seal and add a post-repair hydrogen validation step.
3. Bring the quench control valve back inside 2 °C of setpoint and log response lag weekly.
4. Add an x-ray check on the first part of every pour for the next 30 days.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.body: Synthetic demo data. The ranking is evidence-weighted, not a physical simulation. No automatic line control is performed; the engineer owns the decision.

research.question: Can the next 200 cycles of the Line 6 furnace door seal be predicted with a validated lift over SPC?
research.decision: Stopped: the shadow model showed no validated lift over SPC on the available history. Prediction is not shipped.

checks.label: Define one predictive question with a customer
Baseline survival / gradient boosting vs SPC
checks.note: SPC baseline AUC 0.79; model 0.81, but calibration is poor.

checks.label: Prospective shadow evaluation
checks.note: Six weeks shadow; 0.02 lift, 31% false alarms.

checks.label: Lead time, precision, recall and cost of errors
checks.note: 8 h lead, 31% false alarms, €41k annualised cost of errors.

checks.label: Cost-of-error review with quality and finance
checks.note: No business case at this lift.

checks.label: Product decision: separate, embedded, or stop
checks.note: Stop. Revisit only with more events and a new maintenance-confound strategy.

checks.label: Stop rule: no validated lift over SPC → do not ship
